title: What is known about 1RB0LE_0RC---_1RD0LA_1RE0RA_1LC0LF_0RC1LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_0RC---_1RD0LA_1RE0RA_1LC0LF_0RC1LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, and the machine is not yet analysed. Lean proves no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide); the C simulator finds none in 109. From about step 396,000 the tape has a clear structure: a fixed left end, a counter of 4-cell digits 0110 / 0010 next to it, and to the right a background of 0011 words with sparse defects (0001, alone or doubled) whose spacing grows along the tape. The head returns to the left end only rarely (steps 396,499; 7,742,585; 22,969,011; 86,874,709 among them). Turning this into exact rules is still to do.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (B1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 33,592 cells have been visited and 24,444 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The shape of the tape
claims.text: py/view.py prints the tape each time the head, in state C, reads a 0 on the leftmost visited cell, cut into 4-cell words. After step 396,499 the cells right of the head read: a few cells, a run of 0110 and 0010 words (a counter whose pattern changes between visits), then 0011 words with isolated 0001 defects (o) and doubled ones (oo) at gaps that grow along the tape. Between such visits the head bounces between the right end, which moves right by a few cells each bounce, and turning points at the defects, which drift left. Before step 396,000 the tape is mostly 1s with scattered 0s, another regime.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.495).

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.77×10<sup>10</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 1.77×1010 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 6 checkpoints, the last at 1.00×1010 steps. No trip-level jump was used in this run, only the shift rules over repeated words (exact by induction, but the program is not verified).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts only on B reading 1, that is after A reads a 0 that has a 1 to its right (A>0 1). The next step is to find exact rules for the head's bounce over the 0011 background and its defects, and for the counter.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0RF_1LC0RD_1LA0LD_1LE0RA_0LB---_0LB1RB up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows, and this one has not yet been taken apart. After a messy start the tape settles into a regular texture, a background of 0011 words with sparse defects next to a counter, and the head bounces over it. Only bounded runs are proved so far.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.495).
After 109 steps the tape spans 33,592 cells (99 left of the start, 24,664 right), with a density of 1s of 0.728.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A background with defects
html: The left end of the visited tape stops moving early; the right end keeps growing, about as the square root of the step count. From step 396,499 on, cut the tape into 4-cell words starting just right of the left end. Almost every word is 0011 (written . below), with a few 0001 defects (o), alone or in pairs, and next to the left end a run of 0110 and 0010 words that acts as a counter. Part of the tape at step 7,742,585:

The spacing between defects grows along the tape, roughly linearly. The head bounces between the right end and turning points at the defects, and the defects drift left from bounce to bounce. The head comes all the way back to the left end only rarely: at steps 396,499, 396,541, 465,987, …, 7,742,585, 22,969,011, 86,874,709. The last gaps between these visits grow by a factor of about 4.

sections.heading: What is proved and what is missing
html: Lean: the halting configurations (kernel), no halt in the first 10,000 steps (kernel) and 107 steps (native_decide). C simulator: no halt in 109 steps.

Missing: everything structural. A macro machine needs exact rules for how the head crosses the 0011 background, how it turns at a defect and moves it, how the right end grows, and how the counter changes when the head reaches the left end. The machine can halt only from A>0 1.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

family: Bouncer with a counter and drifting defects (structure seen, not yet a macro machine)
summary: The tape settles into a background of 0011 words carrying sparse defects, with a counter of 4-cell digits at its fixed left end; the head bounces between the growing right end and the defects. No macro machine yet; only bounded runs are proved.
